en: Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was staying on Mount Potalaka, in the sanctuary of the Noble Avalokiteśvara, upon a divine lion-throne made of precious celestial gems and sapphire, strewn with flowers, together with a great community of monks, numbering about five hundred monks. This is the *Sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhāna-vyūha-sūtra*.

Together with all the Arhats who had exhausted their outflows, attained mastery over the mind, and reached the further shore of the True Dharma; and together with all the Bodhisattvas who had attained great compassion and wisdom, all of whom were bound by only one more birth— whether by two births, three births, ten births, twenty births, thirty births, or a hundred births— and all of whom had attained the eight fruits and dwelt on the ten stages, as follows:
Together with seven hundred bodhisattvas headed by the noble Avalokiteśvara, Mañjuśrī, Vimalaketu, Ratnaśrī, Vajraketu, Vimalaprabha, Candana, and Amṛtaketu; as well as with laymen and laywomen,
and five thousand [beings] from various world-systems who had all received their prophecies and attained meditative absorptions, who had assembled there.

Together with all hundreds of thousands of gandharvas who had attended upon previous buddhas and witnessed the miraculous displays of the Tathāgata, and with all the great yakṣiṇīs who had attained the wisdom of a bodhisattva, received their prophecy, and were irreversible— namely Anaupamya, Vimalaprabhā, Prabhāvatī, and Bhīmaśrī.

He was seated together with the yakṣiṇī headed by her like this, along with eighty great yakṣiṇīs; and with these world-protectors: Śatakratu, Brahmā, Vaiśravaṇa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Virūḍhaka, Virūpākṣa, Maṇibhadraputra, and Pūrṇabhadra.
Then, all of them, knowing that the Tathāgata was seated upon the lion-throne, [honored] the Tathāgata with their respective roots of merit.

Honored, worshipped, circumambulated hundreds of thousands of millions of times, and venerated with divine ornaments, garments, flowers, garlands, incense, ointments, and the sound of music; at that very time, the Blessed One entered the meditative absorption named "Abiding in the Wisdom of Great Compassion for All Sentient Beings."
By the power of that concentration and dhāraṇī, the trichiliocosm great thousandfold world systems were illuminated by its light;
all forms became clearly manifest,
and those beings who were blind from birth saw forms with their eyes.
The deaf heard sounds with their ears;
those afflicted by disease became free from disease;
and the naked were clothed in garments.
The insane regained their mindfulness;
those with impaired bodies became possessed of complete faculties;
and the poor obtained wealth.
Indeed, those beings who were previously deprived of wealth, goods, and enjoyments became endowed with wealth, goods, and enjoyments;
all beings were provided with every happiness and had all their aspirations fulfilled.
Whatever beings there were in the triple-thousand great thousandfold world-system, they all approached the Blessed One with palms joined in reverence to hear the Dharma of instruction.
Those beings who had become gods, having abandoned all divine happiness and practiced the recollection of the Buddha, approached the Blessed One where he was in order to hear the Dharma.
Those beings who had become humans likewise renounced human happiness and approached the Blessed One where he was, desiring to hear the Dharma.

Those beings who were *nāgas*, *yakṣas*, *rākṣasas*, *pretas*, *piśācas*, and *bhūtas*, having attained the recollection of the Buddha (*buddhānusmṛti*), became possessed of a mind of loving-kindness toward all sentient beings; having obtained happiness of body and mind, they approached the Blessed One from that direction in order to hear the Dharma.
Those beings who were born in the world of Yama within the blinding darkness also, through the power of the Buddha, obtained mindfulness for a single moment and recognized one another.
They became completely liberated from the great darkness;
all sentient beings came to possess minds of mutual loving-kindness,
and their secondary afflictions were extinguished.
At that very time, the great earth shook in six ways, rising and falling.
Then, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, seated in that assembly, said this to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Āryāvalokiteśvara:
"Noble son, as this great assembly of great Bodhisattvas is illuminated, the omen for the great assembly is clearly manifest."
The prophecy for many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas has been revealed.
The precursor to the Great Discourse on the Dharma is now manifest.
Noble son, there will be the fulfillment of all aspirations and the attainment of great primordial wisdom for many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas.

Therefore, noble son, having generated compassion for sentient beings, for their benefit and happiness, and for the sake of establishing them in unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, question the Tathāgata. Noble son, there will be sentient beings in the future time, in the final age, who are evildoers, poor, emaciated, with bodies of ugly complexion, oppressed by old age and disease, possessing meager resources, with undeveloped bodies and short lifespans.

O son of good family, for the sake of those of little intelligence who are tormented by passion, hatred, and delusion, entreat the Tathāgata to teach the Dharma; this will be for the long-term benefit, welfare, and happiness of sentient beings, for the pacification of all diseases, and for the warding off of all evils.
"For the sake of pacifying all evils, for the sake of fulfilling all vows, and even unto the attainment of unsurpassed parinirvāṇa.
Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, having looked toward the ten directions, brought to mind as many koṭis of Tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā.
Moving toward where the Blessed One was, he bowed with palms joined, circumambulated him three times, prostrated by means of the five-pointed salutation,
and addressed the Blessed One as follows: "Blessed One,
will there be beings in the future time who are oppressed by old age, sickness, sorrow, death, suffering, and untimely death?"

Emaciated, ill-favored, short-lived, possessing meager enjoyments, and with undeveloped bodies, they will kill one another due to a mind of stinginess and immorality; they will seize one another’s wealth, enjoyments, and power; they will delight in laughter, dance, drama, and play; and they will perceive the impermanent as permanent and the impure as pure.
With that as their cause and that as their basis, those beings will be reborn in various kinds of hells, the animal realm, and the world of Yama.

Therefore, O Blessed One, for their sake, for their welfare, for the fulfillment of all their hopes, up to the attainment of the wisdom of a Tathāgata, for birth in a Buddha-field, and for the warding off of all evil, please speak, Blessed One;
please speak, Sugata! There is no such thing as knowledge for a Tathāgata that is unknown, unseen, unheard, or even unrecognized.

“Blessed One, many bodhisattvas, monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, kinnaras, and others have assembled, desiring to hear this discourse on the Dharma; they have served previous Buddhas and have become endowed with wisdom. Yet, having become hopeless, they will depart. Then that entire assembly, having gathered there, prostrated with the five limbs touching the ground and spoke with one voice as follows:
“Excellent, Blessed One! Speak, Blessed One! Speak, Sugata!

Then the Blessed One, having recognized this request for a second and even a third time, looked toward the ten directions and, with a voice that was beautiful and charming, addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Noble Avalokiteśvara:

“Noble son, there is a samādhi called ‘The Array of the Manifestation of Buddha-fields and the Surveying of Sentient Beings through the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas,’ which was heard by me in the past upon my first generation of the mind of awakening.”
He heard this in the presence of the Tathāgata Sukusumajyotiḥsandarśana;
and at the very moment of hearing the name of that samādhi, ninety koṭis of beings attained the wisdom of a Tathāgata,
and they were all prophesied by the Tathāgatas to attain enlightenment in various buddha-fields.
And I, noble son, have attained the prophecy.
I remember, noble son, through the divine Tathāgata-knowledge, that this Dharma-discourse was spoken for the benefit of sentient beings by thirty thousand Tathāgatas;
in every instance, it was you yourself, Noble Avalokiteśvara, and Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, who requested the Tathāgatas [to teach it].
And when this assembly of all the bodhisattvas who had gathered— along with the assembly of monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen— heard this, they all paid it honor and performed worship.
Thereupon, many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of sentient beings received prophecies and became attainers of the bodhisattva samādhis.

Having attained all their desires and fulfilled all their hopes, they prospered; freed from disease, their roots of merit became fully ripened, and they abandoned all obscurations. Possessing forms that were handsome, gracious, and beautiful to behold, they were enriched with wealth, grain, treasuries, and storehouses.
They were highly esteemed by all kings, princes, and ministers, and were worthy of being venerated by all sentient beings.

Possessing mindfulness and wisdom, endowed with unbreakable faith in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, they will be steadfast, possessing longevity, beauty, splendor, strength, and courage, and will be endowed with the excellence of all supreme qualities;
nor shall they ever experience separation from what is dear, nor the loss of what is dear.
In this way, noble son, those sons of good family or daughters of good family will be endowed with many such virtues.

When they prostrate with the five-fold limb-bow (*pañcamaṇḍala*) before this exposition of the True Dharma, having adorned it with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, parasols, banners, and flags,

and having uttered "Homage to the Buddha," they shall pay homage, offer words of praise, uphold it, recite it, cause others to recite it, write it down, and cause others to write it down, generating a mind of supreme reverence.
In the presence of that Dharma-preacher, they shall in this very life be endowed with all excellent qualities:
handsome, pleasing, beautiful to behold, free from disease, long-lived, possessed of stable intelligence, mindful, and resolute;
[they shall be so] before all kings, all queens, princes, ministers, all enemies, and all sentient beings.
They will become worthy of being rejoiced in, worthy of homage, and worthy of honor;
they will possess abundant wealth and requisites,
and the fragrance of sandalwood will emanate from their mouths.
His eyes will be like blue lotuses;
day and night he shall behold Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
and all his obscurations, including the five deeds of immediate retribution and so forth, shall be exhausted.
The deities will protect him,
and at the time of his death, he will have a vision of the Buddhas and a vision of the Bodhisattvas.
They will not die with envy or a distracted mind;
rather, upon passing away, they will be reborn in the world-system of Sukhāvatī. Noble son, I have prophesied for them a face-to-face prophecy.
They have seen me, honored and revered by me.

They should not give rise to doubt regarding enlightenment concerning those who will uphold this Dharma-discourse, who will honor it, write it down or cause it to be written, recite it, worship it, master it, and hear its name. Having formed the thought, "He is a bodhisattva," they should be honored.

By the power of this samādhi and through hearing it, those [afflictions] resulting from the maturation of his past karma— namely, his physical deformity, lack of wealth, deficiency of intellect, being reviled, separation from loved ones, and the upheaval of his kingdom— were [mitigated]: some by means of a headache,
some by the interruption of food, some by the wearing of coarse clothing, some by the affliction of body and mind, and some by the preparation of a bed of painful contact.
Some will bring all that karmic obscuration to exhaustion through this recitation.

Furthermore, one should generate this thought: "In the past, while wandering in saṃsāra, I accumulated various kinds of evil and unwholesome deeds toward sentient beings; I confess them, I reveal them, and I do not conceal them."

One should generate a mind of unbreakable faith toward the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha. Furthermore, whatever karmic obstruction there may be belonging to that son of good family or daughter of good family which is conducive to the cutting off of wealth, or whatever evil karma has been committed and accumulated against the Buddha, the Dharma, the Saṅgha, the Śrāvakas, the Pratyekabuddhas, or toward one's parents— all that [shall be purified].
It will go to complete exhaustion;
he will become endowed with great sovereignty and prosperity;
and whatever karmic obstructions there may be for that son of noble family or daughter of noble family that are to be experienced as painful sensations in the hells, [they too shall be exhausted].

Whatever leads to separation from loved ones, to being born blind, to becoming a woman, to having both sexual organs, or to rebirth in the world of Yama, as a hungry ghost, or in the animal realm through the power of envy, pride, and anger— all that will be completely exhausted.
In this way, noble son, this samādhi is a mine of all virtues.
Noble sons, there are those who ensure that this Dharma discourse endures for a long time,
and there are protections, shields, and guardians for those noble sons and noble daughters;
they bring about the fulfillment of all qualities and all aspirations, provide great wealth, sovereignty, and happiness, and cause the accomplishment of everything thought of and prayed for.

These dhāraṇī mantra-words bring about the exhaustion of all karma; they pacify all untimely death, bad dreams, and all diseases; they ensure victory in all battles; they bestow longevity, complexion, strength, vigor, and stability; they bring all yakṣas, bhūtas, and humans under one's control; they pacify all fevers and poisons; and they lead even to the attainment of prophecy—having heard, retained, and recited them.
Having honored it, having written it, or having had it written for the sake of preservation—
those sons of good family or daughters of good family obtain all these qualities.
Then, at that time, this great earth shook in six ways.
And that assembled multitude, having covered the Tathāgata with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, and pairs of fine cloths as they had gathered there, gave a cry of "Excellent!
They said: "Excellent, excellent, Blessed One! What are those mantra-words?
*Namaḥ sarvatathāgatānām*. *Tadyathā*: O Buddha, O Subuddha, O Śuddhamate!

O you who look upon the world, who look beyond the world, who observe sentient beings; you who are empowered by the empowerment of all Tathāgatas; you who fulfill all aspirations; O bearer of splendor, who are honored even in the hells; you who bestow the wisdom of the Tathāgata and are sustained by the empowerment of the Tathāgata!
May all the world be happy.
May past karma be exhausted. [This is] my "Nātsehaṃ Mārapati-Śukṣiṇasya Āyaṣadika."
May there be protection from all fears for the great faithful lay disciple Śūlivajra, through the empowerment of the Tathāgata; svāhā!
"Noble sons, these mantra-words have been spoken and empowered by thirty thousand Tathāgatas;

they are now spoken by me as well for the sake, welfare, and happiness of all sentient beings, for their protection, defense, and guardianship, to pacify all diseases, and to ensure rebirth in a Buddha-field."
Whosoever in this assembly should think, "How indeed may I obtain all these qualities spoken by the Tathāgata?
should rise early in the morning with a mind of compassion, a mind of pity, and a mind of loving-kindness toward all sentient beings—
having abandoned envy, pride, hypocrisy, and anger— and with a one-pointed mind, having performed a most magnificent worship of the Buddha, [should direct it] toward the ten directions.

Having paid homage to all the Tathāgatas and having brought their qualities to mind according to one's desire, one should recite the mantra one hundred and eight times and offer a single flower to each Tathāgata. Thereupon, all of that person's aspirations will be fulfilled,
and they will behold the Tathāgata in a dream.
Whatever boon one desires, that one shall obtain;
at the time of death, there will be a vision of the Tathāgata;
and having passed away, one will be reborn in the world-system of Sukhāvatī.
He will be endowed with longevity, strength, complexion, and vigor;
and all his enemies will come under his control.
Furthermore, while this dhāraṇī was being spoken, sixty thousand living beings attained the patient acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
And all were completely liberated from the obstructions of all karma, and all their intentions became fully realized.
Then, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, having surveyed the ten directions, said this to the Blessed One:
"Blessed One, there is a dhāraṇī for Bodhisattvas called 'Fearless Splendor' (*abhayatejas*), which was received by me in the presence of the Tathāgata Abhayavyūharāja."
Having received it, it was revealed to all sentient beings. Furthermore, Blessed One, I do not recall anyone— in whose ear that dhāraṇī has even fallen and entered during a dream—
who would have weakness, affliction, disease, fever, bodily pain, or mental distress in their body.
Whether it be untimely death, water, weapons, poison, *gara*, *ḍākinīs*, spirits (*bhūta*), yakṣas, enemies, humans, or non-humans, it is impossible for them to cause harm or inflict injury.
Therefore, may the Blessed One grant permission that I shall bestow the seal of the Bodhisattva’s vow.

For the sake of those Dharma-preachers, those who listen to the Dharma, those who hear it, those who honor it, those who worship it, those who uphold it, and those who recite it—[these mantras] fulfill all aspirations. Homage to all Buddhas! Homage to all Bodhisattvas and Arhats!
Namely: Oṃ vajradhara vajradhara vajrakāya vajrabala vajrateja hūṃ hūṃ vajrapāṇe.
Obey the command of the Tathāgata! Remember your vow!
Destroy all diseases and all evils!
Grant me the boon as I desire:
"May there be no harm to me, the son of Mārapati Śukṣiṇa, Āyaṣādika Śulivajra; whatever we pray for, may each and every one of those be fulfilled."
He he!
Hurry, hurry! Come, come!
Do not delay!
Reveal the vajra-body! Reveal the vajra-body!
By the empowerment of the Buddha, svāhā!
While this dhāraṇī was being spoken, this great earth rose up and sank down;
all the yakṣas and rākṣasas were bewildered, and all the gods, down to humans and non-humans, were struck with wonder and cried out, "Excellent! Excellent!
"Excellent, excellent, Great Beings! These dhāraṇī mantra-words have been spoken as supremely efficacious."
Then the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi said this to the Blessed One:
"Venerable Blessed One, whoever aspires to the stage of a bodhisattva, or seeks wealth, grain, enjoyments,
sovereignty, kingship, the state of a vidyādhara, or long life, strength, vigor, and longevity, by that person [an image] made of white sandalwood on the eighth day of the bright fortnight..."
Vajradhara should be depicted with a loud laugh (*aṭṭahāsa*), adorned with all ornaments;
he should be fashioned together with the relic in his heart.
One who possesses the relic, Vajradhara, the consoler, the holder of the vidyā, while incense is being burned, should be fashioned by one who is pure and has fasted for a day and night.

Then, on the eighth day, having performed the preliminary sprinkling (*pūrva-seka*) and likewise having made an offering with great quantities of incense, flowers, perfumes, and lamps at a pure site sacred to the Tathāgata, one should perform the recitation (*jāpa*) eight hundred times three times over, and worship the Tathāgata. Having paid homage to all the Tathāgatas and placed four full vases, [one should prepare] a mandala made of red sandalwood.

Having dressed in white garments and with a one-pointed mind, one should offer an oblation of the five flavors, perfumes, wine, and milk-rice in the four directions; then, with eight hundred jasmine flowers, Vajrapāṇi should be invoked until the fifteenth day. Then there will arise a great roar, an earthquake, and rays of light will issue forth.
Then I shall grant whatever boon is desired.
All rites and all undertakings will be accomplished merely by the recitation [of this mantra].
One will be free from disease, long-lived, and liberated from all evil.
One shall obtain a thousand virtues;
at the time of death, one shall see a Buddha,
and I too shall grant a vision of myself.
Then the Blessed One gave his approval, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, Vajrapāṇi! This mudrā is not to be transgressed;
no doubt, no uncertainty, and no hesitation should be entertained toward it by the world together with its gods. III
Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta said this to the Blessed One:
"For what reason, Blessed One, is this samādhi called 'The Array that Manifests Buddha-fields through the Observation of Beings by the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas'?
The Blessed One replied:
Through the empowerment of all Tathāgatas and being empowered by all Bodhisattvas, he attains all samādhis and the gateways of all dhāraṇīs;
he thoroughly knows the mental states and mental factors, as well as the contractions and expansions, of all sentient beings.

Among these beings— whether gods, nāgas, humans, yakṣas, gandharvas, pretas, those born as animals, or those in the world of Yama— some are those who have approached merit and performed good deeds, having attained faith in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha;
while others are those who go to hell, having committed evil deeds and being doers of wickedness.
He teaches the Dharma to those beings who have fallen into evil views, restraining them from all evils;
he establishes them in the enlightenment of a Buddha and fulfills all their aspirations;
he dispels envy, pride, anger, and avarice.
And those beings, having attained serene confidence in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, are reborn in the buddha-fields;
they never experience suffering or mental distress.
Therefore, noble son, this is called the samādhi named "The Array that Reveals the Buddha-fields while Surveying Beings through the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas."
Having heard this, they attain the stage of certainty and non-retrogression.
He asked: "In what sense, Blessed One, do those sons of good family receive their prediction? What is the magnitude of their mass of merit?"
"What is difficult to practice?
Venerable Lord, it is difficult to attain even arhatship, let alone unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
The Blessed One said:

And, noble son, whatever perfection of giving, morality, patience, vigor, meditation, and wisdom I have fulfilled since first generating the mind of awakening; and whatever renunciation of head, hands, feet, eyes, limbs, dear sons, wife, daughters, male servants, and female servants I have performed; and [whatever I have done] for this Dharma discourse—

The accumulation of merit consisting of honoring, revering, copying, having it copied, reading, and receiving [this teaching], as well as the accumulation of merit consisting of proclaiming it to others, and the accumulation of merit consisting of honoring and revering those preachers of the Dharma— compared to that, this former accumulation of merit does not approach even a hundredth part.
"Furthermore, noble son, whatever Dharma I have spoken and mastered, let one honor, revere, respect, and worship it all; having honored it, let one write it down or cause it to be written down.
But whoever writes down or recites this discourse on the Dharma, or worships and proclaims it, will acquire a far greater accumulation of merit than that.
Therefore, the Tathāgata grants him the prophecy of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
For what reason? Because it is difficult to hear, take up, retain, honor, or write down a Dharma discourse of such a nature.
Furthermore, those beings are of evil conduct, delighting in food, drink, laughter, and dance; they perceive the impure as pure and are full of desire, anger, and malice.
Perceiving happiness in what is not happiness, they delight in blows, abuse, threats, and beatings; they will neither understand nor take these to heart.
Due to that ignorance which is the cause of their evil karma, and being taken hold of by unwholesome friends, they are tormented by old age, sickness, grief, and death.
At the time of death, they are utterly distraught; seeing one another hanging from beds that resemble a cemetery, they will produce neither a wholesome thought nor an unshakable faith.

Having passed away from there, they will once again experience sufferings. Noble son, this [teaching] cannot be heard, honored, worshipped, or grasped by those who have not cultivated roots of virtue; nor can it be seen by the Tathāgatas, nor can they receive a prophecy. It cannot be written, nor caused to be written, nor believed, nor can those Dharma-preachers be honored or respected by them.
"Even it would not be possible to worship him, O noble son; for wherever this Dharma-discourse shall circulate, there the work of a Tathāgata will be accomplished.
Then that assembled multitude, as they had gathered, gave their applause, saying, "Excellent!"
Excellent, excellent, Blessed One!

We too, Blessed One, shall honor, revere, and respect the Dharma-preacher and the listener of the Dharma as if they were the Tathāgata himself; we shall provide them with every article of comfort and cause this Dharma-discourse to be widely disseminated and protected, so that this Dharma-discourse may endure for a long time.
Then, at that time, the Blessed One, having surveyed the assembly gathered there, spoke thus:
"Excellent, excellent, noble son! Oh, even in this way you must act."
Becoming indifferent to body and mind, even when subjected to all manner of disturbances, insults, reviling, threats, blows, and abuse, this Dharma discourse must be caused to be heard,
written down, and recited. Furthermore, that Dharma-preacher and Dharma-listener must be attended to with every kind of comfortable provision.
That region, that island, and that city must be protected from all fears, calamities, misfortunes, and afflictions;
and one should constantly and continuously keep that son of good family or daughter of good family in mind.
Then, at that time, the Blessed One spoke these verses:
Listen, son of good family, and be heedful, lest you later come to regret it;
for the appearance of a Buddha is attained only once in hundreds of thousands of millions of eons.
If one hears these qualities and places faith in them, it will not be difficult for such a person to attain this samādhi;
even if one were to give gifts to the supreme among bipeds for as many millions of eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges.

Wealth, grain, as well as clothing and ornaments, perfumes, garlands, and ointments— whatever merit there is for one who, having full faith in this sūtra, hears it, recites it, or causes it to be written down— the measure of that merit cannot be found; and it has been taught by the Sugata that it is immeasurable.
One should always resort to the forest with constant vigilance; one should always meditate on meditation with a focused mind;
one should give gifts, even abandoning one's beloved sons and daughters, as well as one's hands and feet.
Just as someone who upholds this sutra would obtain a specific excellence of merit,
so too the giver of its meaning— this excellent sutra— will always be free from all states of woe.
For one who bestows wealth and grain, indeed, all virtues are not difficult to attain;
neither longevity, strength, nor valor is difficult for him to obtain, who upholds this pure sūtra.
They shall behold the Buddha Amitābha, the Leader; he too has been prophesied by me for the enlightenment of a Buddha.
Not even a trace of evil shall ever exist for him; he shall behold the world-realm of Sukhāvatī.

Whatever karma he may have will always be exhausted within the nest of his mind; even when there is pain in the body or fever in the head, he shall never suffer a downfall. Furthermore, he shall obtain visible qualities, and everything that was thought of and prayed for.
Therefore, those monks and nuns, laymen and laywomen, and kings should always show profound respect to the Dharma-preacher, just as they would toward a Lord of Men, a Tathāgata.
And this sutra should always be upheld, and constant honor should be shown to its upholder; having paid honor with perfumes, garlands, and ointments, one should cause it to be written down.
Do not, in a future time, be afflicted by old age and disease, agitated by many thousands of miseries,
wandering through the hells and among animals, being eunuchs or impotent,
loathsome, born blind, or foul-smelling corpses, and be reborn as women in low-born families.
One who is envious, always acting wickedly, overcome by anger, and possessive—
yet having shown reverence toward the Buddhas and their teachings— is reborn among these very beings.
There, experiencing sufferings, do not later come to feel remorse in the future.
Therefore, whether one always honors him who preserves and proclaims [this teaching], or whether one treats him with abuse, contempt, beating, and binding; [the merit or demerit is equal].
By that very act, he has insulted me alone, even while showing honor to me, the upholder; therefore,
one should always [revere] those Dharma-preachers who uphold, write down, or recite [this teaching].
One should always perform acts of hospitality toward them and speak gentle, sweet words.
Then the noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One and said this to the Blessed One:

"I remember, Blessed One, a dhāraṇī called the 'Miracle of Contemplation' (*vyavalokanaprātihāryā*), which was previously received and heard by me in the presence of the Tathāgata Jñānaketuprabhākara."
Having heard, reflected upon, grasped, retained, recited, honored, written down, and caused to be written down this [teaching], they attain the stage of non-retrogression;
they attain all these qualities spoken by the Tathāgata,
and everything is fulfilled for them according to their aspirations.
All his karmic obstructions go to destruction;
he attains meditative concentration,
and his diseases are eliminated.
"The vision of the Buddha becomes the vision of the Bodhisattva.
The Blessed One gave his approval, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, noble son! Set it forth; it has been empowered by the Tathāgata."
Then the Bodhisattva Āryāvalokiteśvara, having paid homage to all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions, spoke these mantra words:
"Homage to all the Tathāgatas, who fulfill all hopes!"
Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Greatly Compassionate One. It is thus:
*ha ha ha ha*, *mama mama*, *dhiri dhiri*.
O peaceful one, perfectly tranquil, who brings about the destruction of all evils!
Behold me, O Compassionate One; bring the thought of awakening (bodhicitta) to mind!
Look upon me; remember, remember the empowerment of truth that was previously performed by you!
By that truth, fulfill all my aspirations;
purify the buddha-field;
let no one cause me any harm.
Through the empowerment of the Buddha, svāhā! Namely:
Teje teje mahāteje!
Whatever evil conduct of body, evil conduct of speech, or evil conduct of mind I have committed, or whatever poverty I have experienced—may you extinguish that for me!
Behold! Look upon!
I long for the sight of the Tathāgata and the sight of the Bodhisattvas; Dhudhupa! Grant me your vision!
May all my virtues increase! Homage to all the Tathāgatas!
Homage to Avalokiteśvara!
"Remember your vow, O Great Beings!
May the words of the mantra be fulfilled, svāhā!
As this dhāraṇī was being spoken, the great earth shook and a great sound of joyous shouting arose.
And as a divine rain of flowers fell, the entire assembly uttered cries of "Excellent!
saying: "Excellent, excellent! This well-spoken [mantra] by the Mahāsattva fulfills all hopes for the sake of protecting all sentient beings.
Protect us from all fears; O destroyer of all karma, pacifier of death, evil dreams, and the wilderness!"
"We too, all having become [such], shall uphold and honor it.
Avalokiteśvara said:
"O son of good family, whoever should desire these virtues..."
Just as the prophecy proclaimed by the Tathāgata is desired by me,
so too do I desire a direct vision [of him], the attainment of samādhi, the sight of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
the acquisition of wealth and sovereignty, and rebirth in a Buddha-field; therefore, having become pure on the bright fortnight with my limbs well-washed, [I shall perform this rite].

Having observed the Noble Eightfold Fast starting from the eighth day, one should worship that site of earth—which is purified and blessed by the Buddha—with perfumes, flowers, banners, flags, and full water-jars; and having likewise worshipped the Dharma-preacher with various flowers, garlands, and scents, he too, being pure with his body well-bathed and clothed in white garments, should have [the mandala] drawn. These [mantras] are not shared with all sentient beings.

Having cultivated roots of merit, with a mind of loving-kindness toward all sentient beings, a mind of compassion, and a mind of pity, and having established a mind of profound reverence for the Tathāgata as one's teacher, one should write it every day, writing until half the day has passed.
Beginning on the eighth day up to the fifteenth, that same worship should be performed daily.
Then, by this very method, through the mere act of writing it down, his five deeds of immediate retribution and all his misdeeds will go to destruction;
he will increase in wholesome qualities and will become one of ardent vigor.
One will attain physical bliss regarding all phenomena;
passion, hatred, delusion, pride, and anger will become attenuated.

Therefore, having had [the image] written out, one should place an image of the Tathāgata facing eastward together with relics, as well as an image of Avalokiteśvara together with relics, and in that shrine containing the relics, [one should worship] with flowers, incense, perfumes, and lamps.
A more magnificent worship should be performed.
Beginning on the eighth day and continuing until the fifteenth, one should maintain a mind of great compassion for all sentient beings.

Eating pure and white food, observing the noble eightfold fast (*āryāṣṭāṅga-upavāsa*), accompanied by virtuous friends, and having completely abandoned pride, anger, and envy, one should perform increasingly magnificent worship day by day and recite the mantra at the three junctions of the day.
One hundred and eight [offerings] should be given.

Having offered lamps, incense, flowers, perfumes, and so forth, one should circumambulate the image of the Noble Avalokiteśvara three times each at the three junctions of the day with one hundred and eight *sumana* flowers.
And incense should be offered to Vajrapāṇi.

Having paid homage to the ten directions, one should cast an offering of various juices, drinks, curd-rice, and so forth toward the four quarters— behind the goddess Bhīmā, in front of Anopamā, and above Śaṅkhinī.
Then no one will cause him distraction,
nor will even terror arise.
There is no alteration of the mind.
For all [of these], there is a recitation of eight hundred times, and an incitement with eight hundred *sumana* flowers.
Having performed the preliminary sprinkling according to this very procedure, one should then place four full jars on the fifteenth day of the lunar month.

Having offered incense, sandalwood, kunduruka, and camphor, and having adorned that spot of earth with four lamps, various perfumes, banners, cloth streamers, and vessels of gold and silver; having given and presented as an offering in the four directions curds, honey, milk-rice, and boiled rice with curds, along with whatever else is available; and having recited the mantra once over eight hundred *sumana* flowers, they should be scattered in the four directions.
As before, reciting the mantra one hundred and twenty-four times for each, one should bring forth an image of the noble Avalokiteśvara using very fragrant *jāti* flowers;
then that true image will tremble and a great sound will arise.
Rays of light will issue forth,
and an earthquake will occur;
thereafter, all his actions and all his undertakings will reach fulfillment.
Having a vision of the Tathāgata, he will attain the stages of a bodhisattva and become worthy of the veneration of all sentient beings;
he will be enriched with wealth, grain, treasuries, and granaries, be free from all diseases, and live for a long time.

All enemies will desire to see all kings, princes, and ministers; they will become well-disposed, having abandoned all afflictions, passion, hatred, and delusion. There shall never be separation from those dear to them.

Endowed with great, firm strength and vigor, majestic, sharp in faculties, wise, possessing a mind of compassion for all beings, and knowing the Dharma, until the time of their passing, [they shall behold] the Buddha, the Blessed One, and the Noble Avalokiteśvara.
He sees that one who dwells in loving-kindness passes away;
while teaching the Dharma, he is reborn in whichever Buddha-fields or families of great universal monarchs he desires, wherever he directs his mindfulness.

And he shall obtain many thousands of other virtues as well. Thus, Blessed One, this Dharma discourse produces manifold benefits. These dhāraṇī-mantra words of yours cannot be heard, nor retained, nor honored, nor written, nor caused to be written, without the empowerment of the Tathāgata.
It is not possible to have faith.
If there were seeing, there would be no hearing;
if there were hearing, one would listen with a distracted mind, and thus would not have faith and would not show respect.
If one honors [this scripture] with a mind of affliction and malice, or if one writes it or causes it to be written with a distracted mind—
why is that?
Because, due to the cause of the fruit of their former evil karma, they must experience the result of that karma.
He will fall into doubt;
he will commit one of the five deeds of immediate retribution;
yet, through three means of accomplishment, all his aspirations will be fulfilled.
"No doubt, no uncertainty, and no hesitation should be raised here.
Then the Blessed One gave his approval to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara:
"Excellent, excellent, noble son!"
"This Dharma discourse shall perform the work of a Tathāgata for all sentient beings.
Then, indeed, the great yakṣiṇī Anopamā approached the place where the Blessed One was.
Having covered the Blessed One with various flowers and pairs of fine garments, he prostrated at the Blessed One’s feet and addressed him thus:
“I recall this, Blessed One: while the Blessed One was staying in Kauśāmbī at Ghoṣila’s Grove, I made a vow before him for the sake of all sentient beings.
I too, Blessed One, know the heart-mantra of all the vidyādharas.”
May the Blessed One grant me permission for this, for the benefit of many, for the happiness of many, and for the sake of fulfilling all hopes of the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen.
Homage to all the Tathāgatas! Namely: *ha ha*, *hī hī*.
Hu hu / sara sara / lahuṃ lahuṃ.
Quickly, quickly!
O Great Vidyā, you who are honored by all the vidyādharas!
Hasaḥ hasaḥ!
Why do you stand? Why do you stand?
O you whose limbs are adorned with ornaments variegated with gold! Paṭa paṭa! Bhara bhara!
Bhiri bhiri!
Bhūru bhūru!
Accomplish all my aims!
Turu turu! Accomplish the purpose! Grant me the purpose!
I am unable to endure the lord of Māra;
[for all the Saṅghas], success! Alas, alas! Padme, Padme, Mahāpadme!
O pure one, O very pure one, O great pure one!
Be, be, for the arising from existence! To that terrible one, to that terrible one, I bow! To that terrible one, to that terrible one, I bow!
Therefore, employ this knowledge for me;
bring about its accomplishment; fulfill all my aspirations through the empowerment of the Buddha, svāhā!

Whoever desires the qualities of the Blessed One, desires wealth and grain, desires to bring all sentient beings under their control, or who longs for great sovereignty, kingship, or the state of a Vidyādhara— such a person shall obtain a direct vision of me as well. On the eighth day of the waxing moon, a pure painter, having fasted according to the noble eightfold precepts, [should paint] on a new cloth with uncut fringes and free of hair.
It should be painted with limbs joined together, arranged within nine vessels.

In the center is an image of the Tathāgata teaching the Dharma; to the right is the Noble Vajrakrodha, brandishing a vajra, adorned with all ornaments, wearing flower garlands and a crescent-moon necklace, and clothed in white garments; on the left side—

[She is] incomparable, white as a reed-stalk, adorned with all ornaments, wearing white garments, holding a lotus in her hand, and offering consolation. Then, a pure vidyādhara, having observed the noble eightfold fast, at a pure site of a Tathāgata containing relics, subsisting on milk and barley-gruel,

dressed in white garments, accompanied by a second person, and having performed the preliminary sprinkling on the eighth day [of the lunar fortnight], [should worship] with various flowers, perfumes, incense, and lamps.
Having performed the worship, one should recite the mantra three times, eight hundred times each.

Reciting over each individual *sumana* flower, one should collect those flowers for the image by the number of eight hundred and three. First, flowers, incense, and perfumes should be offered to the Tathāgata and Vajrapāṇi.
As for the sacrificial offering (*bali*), there should be milk-rice, curd-rice, various flavors, and various kinds of liquor.
It should be thrown in the four directions.

On the full moon of the fifteenth day, by this very rite, the *bali* offering and other items—such as incense, camphor, *kunduruka*, sandalwood, and ointments—should be given according to what is available.
Two lamps should be offered with fragrant oil.

There I shall appear in my own form and grant whatever boon is desired: the attainment of meditative concentration, the power of traveling through the sky, invisibility, kingship, the status of a powerful universal monarch (*balacakravartin*), the state of a knowledge-holder (*vidyādhara*), the science of hidden treasures (*nidhivāda*), the science of alchemy (*dhātuvāda*), knowledge of the minds of others, and long life.
One should maintain a mind of loving-kindness toward all sentient beings;
one should be free from pride, anger, envy, and avarice; one should refrain from misappropriating the property of a stūpa, the property of the Dharma, or the property of the Saṅgha;
and one should possess unshakable faith in the Tathāgatas.

And if, O Blessed One, I should commit one of the five deeds of immediate retribution and you do not attend to me with these three means, may I not, O Blessed One, awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment— provided that there should be anyone who has failed to gain faith in the Buddha,

or who has fallen into doubt, or who, having committed evil and unwholesome deeds, does not embrace restraint, and whose mind is possessed by the afflictions and secondary afflictions. For such a person, I [would not attain awakening].
"I shall grant you a vision and I shall also bring about your attainment.
Then the Blessed One gave his approval, saying,
"Excellent, excellent, sister!"
Excellent indeed, sister, that for the sake of all sentient beings you have spoken these such mantra-words and made this vow toward beings of evil conduct.
By means of such great compassion as this, you will be able to establish all sentient beings in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"In the same way, you too must act.
Then the Great Goddess Śaṅkhinī, having worshipped the Blessed One with various flowers and various perfumes, and having circumambulated him, prostrated at his feet and said this to the Blessed One:
"I too, Blessed One, through the empowerment of the Tathāgata, shall make a vow for the sake of the long endurance of the Tathāgata’s teaching."
And I shall provide for those Dharma-preachers and listeners of the Dharma the mantra-words that fulfill all their aspirations;
may the Blessed One grant me permission for this protection.
Homage, homage to all the Tathāgatas!
Oṃ, Goddess Śaṅkhinī, come, come!
Stay, O Wealth, Conqueror of Wealth!
Vṛ vṛ vṛ, you who cause increase!
Dhṛ dhṛ, O bestower of fortitude! O wearer of various and manifold garments, ornaments, and weapons! Yu yu, O protector of life!
Remember the Bodhicitta of the Tathāgatas; do not delay! Grant me this boon! Śaṅkhini svāhā!
By means of these mantra-words, O Blessed One, when applied to the body, one shall attain an increase in fame;
an increase in splendor, an increase in enjoyments, an increase in sovereignty, long life, and an increase in the subjugation of enemies.

Having offered a bali-oblation with whatever is available while reciting [the mantra] one hundred and eight times, one should likewise offer incense of *kunduruka* in the four directions and perform a most magnificent worship of the Tathāgata.
A lamp should be offered.
For twenty-one days, one should abide in loving-kindness and remain established in the observance.
Thereafter, I shall fulfill every intention, with the exception of those who reject the true Dharma.
"It should be performed in a clean place or in a temple.
Then the Blessed One and that assembled multitude gave their approval, saying,
"Excellent, excellent, sister!"
This is well-spoken;
your vow is endowed with many virtues.
In this very way, you too must act in the future time. VI

Then the Great Goddess Bhīmā, having honored the Blessed One with golden flowers and prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One, addressed the Blessed One as follows: "O Blessed One, for the sake of those Dharma-preachers, those listeners of the Dharma, those scribes, those who uphold it, those who recite it, and those who worship it, I shall [bestow] mantras that fulfill all hopes, which grant gold, jewels, pearls, enjoyments, sovereignty, kingship, and long life."
I shall give you the mantra syllables for subjugating enemies.

Whatever king or queen, monk or nun, layman or laywoman, shall uphold, honor, write, or cause to be written [this], and shall practice it as instructed with the profound reverence due to a Tathāgata, they will attain success.
O Blessed One, I shall protect him, I shall provide for his preservation, I shall grant him appropriate boons, I shall ensure he lacks nothing in terms of enjoyments and sovereignty,
I shall secure victory for him in disputes, battles, riots, and tumults,
and I shall bestow upon him a fullness of lifespan.
"And I shall provide protection for that district and city;
may the Blessed One grant me permission for this.
Homage to all the Tathāgatas, to all the Bodhisattvas, beginning with the noble Avalokiteśvara and Vajrapāṇi."
Oṃ, O Great Goddess, terrible one of terrifying intellect!
Victorious one, bringer of victory!
O you who possess the speed of fame, the speed of splendor!
O you who have attained the prophecy, who behold all sentient beings, and who abound in the splendor of compassion, uphold that which is authorized by the Tathāgata! Remember your vow!
By the empowerment of the Buddha, grant me this boon!
Accomplish the siddhi!
O Goddess, Great Goddess, Goddess of True Speech, O Bhīme, established in true speech, dweller in the secret place, svāhā!
Blessed One, these mantra-words, empowered by the Tathāgata and authorized by the Tathāgata, have been spoken by me for the benefit of sentient beings.

Whatever desire one may have in mind, having recited [the mantra] before the Tathāgata after making offerings of flowers, incense, perfumes, and lamps, and having given an offering of milk-rice and a *bali* in the four directions,

I shall fulfill every hope through eight hundred recitations of that very [mantra]. Whoever should desire me in my own form, by him— on the eighth day, when the hair has been removed, the fingernails untrimmed, and with limbs free from ointments, using nine vessels— [the rite should be performed].
It should be painted by a skilled artist endowed with the noble eightfold path: [the goddess] white as a reed-stalk, her limbs adorned with all ornaments and clad in white garments;
in the center, an image of the Tathāgata teaching the Dharma; to the right, the noble Avalokiteśvara engaged in conversation; and on the left side, the great goddess Bhīmā.

Attended by Kuṇḍikā and Netṛkā, she offers consolation. Then, on the eighth day, having performed the preliminary sprinkling, at the site of the reliquary containing the relics, with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, and ointments,
and with offerings of rice-porridge mixed with curd toward the four directions, a pure Vidyādhara performs this most magnificent rite until the fifteenth day of the full moon.
Having performed worship with flowers, incense, perfumes, and lamps, and having offered a bali-oblation with various flavors and other items as available—
including a white bali— having become possessed of a mind of loving-kindness and compassion toward all sentient beings, one should take hold of that image with eight hundred jasmine flowers.

For each individual recitation performed there, I shall manifest in my own form and grant whatever boon is desired: royal sovereignty, the power of traveling through the sky, the science of hidden treasures (*nidhivāda*), the science of alchemy (*dhātuvāda*), the state of a *vidyādhara*, and other activities as desired,
including the prevention of untimely death, the pacification of all diseases, the crushing of enemy armies, and the obtaining of a son.
May there be the arrival of wealth and joy for all sentient beings.

O Bhagavat, if I should commit the five deeds of immediate retribution and yet fail to fulfill every aspiration, may I not awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment— excepting only those who reject the true Dharma and those who have fallen into doubt.
"In the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha.
The Blessed One said:

"Excellent, excellent, sister! It is indeed excellent, sister, that you have set out for the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings, and for the sake of the long endurance of this very Dharma-discourse."
"You have set out [on this path].
Therefore, sister, you must always keep these vows constantly in mind."
Then, at that time, this great earth trembled and a divine rain of flowers fell from above.
And that entire assembly gave a cry of "Excellent!
saying, "Excellent, excellent! This is well-spoken."
The vow shall fulfill all hopes for all sentient beings.

Then, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara again addressed the Blessed One: "Furthermore, Blessed One, what [merit] will that son of good family or daughter of good family obtain through writing, reciting, causing to be written, proclaiming, reading, studying, honoring, and making known [this sūtra]?"
"One shall obtain merit from this Dharma-discourse.
The Blessed One said:
"In that case, Noble Avalokiteśvara, I shall question you; answer as you see fit."
Avalokiteśvara said:
"May the Blessed One himself explain; for there is nothing that the Tathāgata has not seen, has not heard, or has not cognized.
The Blessed One said:

And, noble son, the merit that one shall obtain from writing down this Dharma-discourse, having it written down, reciting it, honoring it, proclaiming it, reading it, and studying it, cannot be described even by way of analogy. For what reason?
Having given gifts that fulfill the intentions of all sentient beings, those beings remain indeed unliberated from aging, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, dejection, and despair.

Even after being made to sport with the five strands of sensual pleasure for a thousand years, those beings remain indeed unliberated; they once again experience sufferings in the realms of hell-beings, animals, the world of Yama, and hungry ghosts.

Having caused sentient beings to hear this Dharma-discourse, having performed worship and its proclamation, and having understood its meaning, they practice it through actual application; thus, they become completely liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, dejection, and despair, and from all the hells, the animal realm, and the world of Yama.
Therefore, the Tathāgatas do not establish a measure for this mass of merit even by means of a simile.
And whichever son of good family, for the sake of this Dharma-discourse, should renounce even as much gold as a mustard seed,

or a single flower, or a single fruit, or a single banner, or music, or incense, or clothing, or a seat, or an ornament, and should write it, cause it to be written, preserve it, recite it, worship it, honor it, and [share it] with others—
One who would fully proclaim this in detail, and who would cause that Dharma-preacher to recite it, and worship him; and one who, while the Tathāgata remains present,
would worship and honor him together with his assembly with face-to-face offerings, attending upon him for a hundred thousand years with every kind of comfortable provision,
with perfumes, garlands, ointments, banners, and flags, and would have monasteries, walkways, and gardens constructed rising half a yojana high— [the latter would generate greater merit].

If one were to cause a hundred or a thousand stūpas made of the seven precious gems to be constructed for the sake of the Tathāgata, and were to honor them with divine offerings for a hundred thousand years, this [latter act] would produce a far greater accumulation of merit than that;
for by writing down, causing to be written, upholding, reciting, honoring, and proclaiming this Dharma-discourse, one does not [attain such merit] as this.
Making offerings in the presence of the Tathāgata is far superior to giving gifts to sentient beings and causing them to enjoy the five strands of sensual pleasure.
Therefore, those sons of good family or daughters of good family, as well as kings, princes, high officials, and ministers, should constantly honor this Dharma discourse with flowers;
they should conceive of it as being the Tathāgata himself.
One should listen to, take up, uphold, recite, and attend to this Dharma-discourse with reverence toward those spiritual friends who cause one to hear it, explain it, and provide its meaning;
and one should generate such a thought as follows:
(Dutt 80) We have gained a great gain; we have obtained what is well-obtained,

in that he who shows the path to those traveling on a wrong path— who perceive what is not beneficial as beneficial, what is impermanent as permanent, and what is not pleasant as pleasant— has done so for the sake of our liberation from the realms of hell, the animal womb, and the world of Yama.
"The work of the Tathāgata has been accomplished.
Avalokiteśvara said,
"By means of this great work, the work of the Tathāgata, this Dharma-discourse has been revealed for the sake of all sentient beings."
The Blessed One said:
"And this Dharma-discourse, noble son, will circulate in the southern region during the final period, in the final age;
there too, monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, kings, princes, high officials, and ministers will become worthy vessels and its worshippers."
They will become holders and reciters; they will have faith and conviction.
However, if it should circulate in the north, east, west, or south, those beings there will be occupied with other activities;

they will not hear it, will not have faith, will not have conviction, and will not honor it. They will be of inferior energy, with lost mindfulness, their thoughts distracted by various diversions, household affairs, male and female servants, enjoyments, power, laughter, play, drama, song, envy, and stinginess.

They will not hear it, they will not believe it, and they will not honor it; thus, they will remain utterly unliberated from old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, dejection, and despair, as well as from the realms of the hungry ghosts and the world of Yama.
Therefore, those sons of good family or daughters of good family who desire to liberate themselves from all states of woe—
This Dharma-discourse should be honored, worshipped, upheld, revered, and proclaimed to others;
it should be maintained in the mind.

[It protects] from tumults, disturbances, bad dreams, and ill omens; and from untimely death, the death of cattle, the death of livestock, the death of humans, and from the perils and afflictions of various diseases.

Having honored this Dharma-discourse, it should be recited; or, having raised it upon a banner and honored it with various perfumes, flowers, incense, and musical instruments, one should exert oneself.
Having offered an oblation in the four directions and paid homage with flowers, incense, and perfumes, all calamities will be pacified.
Then, at that time, the Blessed One spoke these verses:
"For the sake of favoring all sentient beings, those [teachings] which were spoken by the Leaders in previous existences."
"I shall teach you likewise; Ānanda, take up this samādhi. (Stav 1)

Even if one were to fill the threefold world with the seven precious jewels and give them as a gift, while remaining ever heedful toward the Buddhas and the Dharmas, that gift would not equal even a fraction of this [practice]. (Stav 2)

And whoever, having placed deep faith in the Buddhas, should have monasteries and shrines built, and whoever should uphold even a single sūtra—this latter person shall possess far more merit than that. (Stavaka 3)
And whoever should cast down even a single flower, a cloth, a garland, or likewise an ointment, and should honor this samādhi—this latter person's merit is far greater than that. (Stav 4)
And whoever should give a gift of a kārṣāpaṇa coin for the sake of honoring this sūtra,
having generated a mind of loving-kindness directed toward awakening, would obtain much more merit than that. (Stav 5)

And whatever bodhisattva should illuminate and teach this samādhi among sentient beings, and likewise establish them in unsurpassed awakening—even for such a person, there is no comparison for their merit. (Stavaka 6)
Having heard this and likewise having cultivated loving-kindness toward all sentient beings,
one should therefore uphold this sutra, write it down, recite it, and likewise proclaim it. (Stav 7)
Afflicted by old age, sickness, and death, as well as by hundreds of such extremely intense sufferings, and being reborn in the hells and among the hungry ghosts—do not later feel remorse! (Stav 8)
At the time of death, his mind terrified by fear, repeatedly gasping for breath, that one of childish intellect looks from face to face, wondering, "Who will be my protection and my refuge? (Stava 9)
(Dutt 85) "Since, having paid honor to the Tathāgata, as well as to the Buddha's Dharma and the Saṅgha,
one shall steal from them and lead them away to the terrible world of Yama— for such a person there will never be any protection whatsoever. (Stav 10)

Having abandoned wife and children, as well as friends and kinsmen, neither kingdom nor jesting and dance, nor wealth, nor grain, nor clothing and ornaments—having renounced all that which is again harsh with suffering. (Stava 11)
Having no faith in this samādhi, one experiences such terrible suffering as this.
Having heard of this suffering and these benefits, what person of immature intellect would not develop serene confidence? (Stav 12)
Therefore, those monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, and kings should always uphold this sutra and constantly show honor to its upholders. (Stav 13)
Then the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:
"I have grasped this Dharma-discourse, O Blessed One; I shall uphold it with the perception of it as the Teacher, I shall honor it, and I shall proclaim it to all sentient beings.
The Blessed One said:
"Ānanda, if you were to hear all the Dharma that has been spoken by me and yet did not retain it all,

nor recite it, nor honor it, nor propagate it, you would not have offended me, nor would you have failed to listen, nor would you have ceased to be a disciple. But he who does not retain this Dharma-discourse [would indeed be at fault]."

If one were not to recite it, nor worship it, nor proclaim it, nor attend to it in the mind, that person would be at fault toward me; it would constitute a failure to listen, and it would result in a state of non-discipleship.
Therefore, Ānanda, you must preserve this Dharma discourse with reverence.
In the future time, in the final age, this will perform for you the work of a Tathāgata in attaining unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment for the sake of all sentient beings.

Furthermore, while this Dharma discourse was being spoken by the Blessed One, the minds of sixty thousand living beings were liberated from the outflows through non-clinging; seven hundred [beings] attained the samādhis of a bodhisattva;
and five hundred [beings] received prophecies regarding various buddha-fields.
Ninety thousand living beings were completely liberated from all afflictions, and all their unfavorable conditions, states of woe, and miserable rebirths were abandoned.
Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara again addressed the Blessed One:

"Blessed One, in the future time, in the final age, this Dharma discourse shall perform the work of a Tathāgata for those sons of good family who hear it, uphold it, honor it, and likewise for those who write it down."
They shall act;
they have been prophesied for various Buddha-fields according to their wishes.
And as for those beings in the future time, in the final age, who are full of various distractions such as laughter, dancing, singing, and instrumental music—
Blinded by passion, hatred, and delusion, perceiving pleasure and play where there is none, and perceiving permanence in what is impermanent, they— possessed by envy, stinginess, and immorality—
will not honor, will not revere, will not have faith in, will not trust, will not uphold, will not listen to, and will not practice through actual application.
Having exhausted that previous fruit of their wholesome karma, they will experience various sufferings and mental distresses—
the sufferings of hell. Then, after experiencing suffering for many hundreds of billions of eons, they will be reborn in the hells, the animal realm, or the world of Yama.
For a long time they will be under the influence of unwholesome friends and will later feel regret, having squandered this present opportunity.
Therefore, you must practice restraint of body, speech, and mind;

you must possess unshakable faith in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha; and you must maintain a mind of loving-kindness toward all sentient beings, remaining free from envy, stinginess, and immoral thoughts, and free from anger.
Then that assembled multitude, having gathered together, honored the Tathāgata with various meritorious deeds:

with divine flowers, perfumes, garlands, ointments, garments, and ornaments; with shouts of "kilikili" and "prakṣveḍita"; and with the music of celestial instruments, cymbals, and songs, they offered their acclamation, saying: "Excellent, excellent, Blessed One! This great discourse on the Dharma has been well-spoken for the benefit of all sentient beings, so that the teaching of the Tathāgata may endure for a long time."
Then the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:
"Blessed One, what is the name of this Dharma-discourse, and how, Blessed One, should we remember it?
The Blessed One said:
Therefore, Ānanda, you should remember this Dharma-discourse by the name "The Progression through the Bodhisattva Stages of the Wisdom of All Tathāgatas";
remember it also by the name "The Great Assembly of the Self-Existent Ones’ Miraculous Transformations";
and remember it also by the name "The Array of the Manifestation of Buddha-fields and the Surveying of Beings through the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas."
Thus spoke the Blessed One.

The noble Avalokiteśvara, Mañjuśrī, Vajrapāṇi, and all the other bodhisattva mahāsattvas, as well as all the great śrāvakas, and all the Śakras, Brahmās, and world-protectors, and the four [great kings], were uplifted in spirit.

The great kings, the great yakṣiṇīs— such as Anaupamya, Vimalaprabhā, Prabhāvatī, Bhīmā, Śrī, Śaṅkhinī, Haritā, and Mahādevī— as well as the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, and that entire assembly gathered there, having rejoiced in what the Blessed One had spoken, gave their approval, saying: "Excellent, excellent, Blessed One!"
[Thus ends the Mahāyāna sūtra titled "The Array of the Manifestation of Buddha-fields through the Observation of Beings by the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas"].
